title: The store, from scratch
objective: Understand what a zustand store actually is — a closure over a state value and a Set of listeners — and how set/get/subscribe work, with zero React involved.

quiz.prompt: In this codebase (zustand 5.x), `createStore` builds an `api` object literal and returns it. Which list is EXACTLY the set of methods on that object, nothing more and nothing less?

options.text: `setState`, `getState`, `subscribe`, `getSnapshot`
`setState`, `getState`, `getInitialState`, `dispatch`
`setState`, `getState`, `subscribe`, `destroy`
`setState`, `getState`, `getInitialState`, `subscribe`

quiz.prompt: The store holds `{ value: 1, other: 'a' }` and one listener is subscribed. You call `setState({ value: 1 })` with no second argument. What happens?

options.text: The listener runs once: the guard compares the partial's reference to the current state before any merge, so a fresh object never bails out even with identical content
Nothing happens: the merge runs first and yields an object whose contents equal the current state, so the guard treats the update as unchanged and never notifies
Nothing happens: the guard shallow-compares each top-level key of the partial against the current state, finds `value` unchanged, and skips the update
The listener runs once, but receives the same state reference for both arguments, because merging a key that did not change returns the existing object

quiz.prompt: State is `{ nested: { count: 0, label: 'x' }, other: 5 }`. You call `set((s) => ({ nested: { count: s.nested.count + 1 } }))`. What is the state afterwards?

options.text: `{ nested: { count: 1, label: 'x' }, other: 5 }`
`{ nested: { count: 1 }, other: 5 }`
`{ nested: { count: 1, label: 'x' } }`
`{ nested: { count: 1 }, label: 'x', other: 5 }`

quiz.prompt: State is the object `{ a: 1 }`. Which single call leaves `getState()` returning exactly `null` afterwards?

options.text: `setState({}, true)`, passing an explicit `replace` of true
`setState((s) => ({ ...s, a: null }))`, passing no `replace`
`setState(null)`, passing no second `replace` argument at all
`setState(null, false)`, passing an explicit `replace` of false

quiz.prompt: You create `createStore(() => initial)` with `initial = { value: 1 }`, then call `setState({ value: 2 })` and later `setState({ value: 3 })`. What does `getInitialState()` return now, and what does calling it cost?

options.text: A structural clone of `{ value: 1 }` taken at creation time, so it is equal to `initial` but never the identical object
The current state `{ value: 3 }`, because the initial snapshot is re-pointed at the newest state on every successful set
A fresh `{ value: 1 }` produced by re-invoking the state creator, so each call runs your initializer one more time
The very same `initial` object reference captured when the creator ran; the state creator is never invoked again
